title: Wife Of IPS Officer Who Died By Suicide Accuses Haryana Top Cop Of Abetment: 'Well-Planned...' | India News - News18
text: Amneet P Kumar, an IAS officer and wife of late IPS officer Y Puran Kumar, who died by suicide from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, has filed a police complaint seeking an FIR against Haryana Director General of Police (DGP) Shatrujeet Kapur and Rohtak Superintendent of Police (SP) Narendra Bijarniya. In her complaint, filed after returning from an official trip to Japan on Wednesday, Kumar alleged that DGP Kapur and SP Bijarniya were part of a “well-planned conspiracy" to falsely implicate her husband in a “frivolous and mischievous complaint" through fabricated evidence. Y Puran Kumar, a senior Haryana IPS officer, who died by suicide at his Sector 11 residence in Chandigarh, reportedly cited “mental harassment" by senior officials, police sources said while speaking to News18 earlier this week. Meanwhile, a senior Haryana police official denied Amneet Kumar’s allegations and told the Indian Express that these were a response to the government’s “crackdown on corruption". Sources told News18 on Wednesday that Kumar was distressed after his name appeared in a bribery case filed by a liquor contractor without the state government’s authorisation. Kumar, a 2001-batch IPS officer, had been transferred on September 29 to the Police Training College in Sunaria, Rohtak, shortly before his death. He had earlier served as Inspector General of the Rohtak Range. Born on May 19, 1973, the officer held an engineering degree and was due to retire in May 2033. In a note recovered after his death, Kumar reportedly named ten senior officers, both serving and retired, alleging sustained psychological harassment and a conspiracy to damage his career. Reports by the Indian Express also said that Kumar accused them of “caste-based discrimination, public humiliation, targeted mental harassment and atrocities".
